rules.name: Focus Area Requirement
rules.desc:
As part of the MATSCI bachelor’s degree, students complete a Focus Area of study based on their interests within Materials Science and Engineering and its intersection with other fields. Typically, students take courses that bridge their academic, technical, and research interests to build on knowledge gained through the Fundamentals and Depth requirements. Students can select three courses from one of the Focus Area Tracks below or define their own Focus Area based on their interdisciplinary interests. Recommendations for Science courses are at the bottom of each Focus Area Track to help prepare students for further coursework.

• Choose one of the nine focus area tracks listed below or the self-defined focus area option.

• Select three (3) courses within one of the focus areas for a minimum of 9 units.

• At least one course for the focus area must be a MATSCI course.

• Each focus area course must be at least three units and may not include seminars.

• The self-defined focus area option requires additional approval; program deviation forms for this option can be found on the MATSCI website.

*For additional information and sample, programs see the Handbook for Undergraduate Engineering Programs.
rules.notes: Honors Program: For students pursuing the Honor’s Program, you may count up to six units of MATSCI 150 toward the focus area but cannot use these units to replace the MATSCI course minimum.

children.name: Biological Properties of Materials
children.notes:
CHEM 31A and B or CHEM 31M recommended
Students pursuing this focus area will learn more about biocompatible, biomimetic, or even naturally occurring biological materials, along with how they can be engineered.

children.name: Chemical Properties of Materials
children.notes:
CHEM 31A and B or CHEM 31M recommended
Students pursuing this focus area will learn about the thermodynamic principles governing materials, the chemistry involved in synthesizing materials, and the design of the systems and processes necessary to create them.

children.name: Computational Materials Science
children.notes:
PHYSICS 41, 43, and 45 recommended
Students pursuing this focus area will learn more about computational methods used to study materials structure-property relationships and how to make materials predictions.

children.name: Electronics & Photonics Properties of Materials
children.notes:
PHYSICS 41, 43, and 45 recommended
Students pursuing this focus area will learn more about the design and function of electronic and/or photonic devices, as well as the underlying principles of physics relevant to their operation.

children.name: Materials for Energy Technology
children.notes:
Either Physics or Chemistry
Students pursuing this focus area will learn more about materials used in modern energy technologies, potentially including solar cells, wind turbines, batteries, and fuel cells, as well as other emerging energy production or storage devices.

children.name: Materials Characterization
children.notes:
Either Physics or Chemistry
Students pursuing this focus area will learn more about the tools and techniques used in advanced materials characterization, particularly at the micro- and nanoscale.

children.name: Mechanical Behavior & Materials Processing
children.notes:
PHYSICS 41, 43, and 45 recommended
Students pursuing this focus area will learn more about the mechanical behavior of materials, including how to characterize them, and how these mechanical properties influence the design of technologies.

children.name: Materials Physics
children.notes:
PHYSICS 61 and Physics 81 recommended, with Physics 45 or Physics 71 as the science elective.
Students pursuing this focus area will gain a deep foundational knowledge of materials physics, with topics focusing on quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, and waves and diffraction, and other advanced topics.

children.name: Nanomaterials & Nanotechnology
children.notes:
Either Physics or Chemistry
Students pursuing this focus area will learn more about how materials properties change at the nanoscale, including the new and interesting ways in which these changes can be exploited for novel technologies.

children.name: Self-Defined Focus
children.notes:
Either Physics or Chemistry
Students may also define their own focus area containing a minimum of 9 units (3 courses) that comprise a cohesive program of study. Many students use this option to create an interdisciplinary focus area that combines parts of the listed focus area options above. Students should also choose this option if including courses not listed in one of the focus area tracks and should include a petition form along with their final program sheet when conferring their degree.

children.name: Research-Based Track
children.desc:
Complete at least two consecutive quarters of independent research within the same research group.
Students are expected to participate in either the annual Materials Science and Engineering Research Symposium or an alternative approved public oral/poster presentation.
Students who choose this option are strongly encouraged to pursue the honors in the major. More information can be found below.

children.name: Internship-Based Track
children.desc: Complete at least 4 quarters of MATSCI 169 (1 unit per quarter for a total of 4 units). Students are expected to enroll in both Spring and Autumn quarter offerings, bridging their summer internship twice. Following the internship, students complete a research report outlining their work activity, problems investigated, key results, and any follow-on projects they expect to perform.

rules.name: Honors Program Overview
rules.desc:
The Materials Science and Engineering Honors Program offers an opportunity for undergraduate Materials Science and Engineering majors with a GPA of 3.7 or higher to pursue independent research at an advanced level, supported by a faculty advisor and graduate student mentors. The main requirements are as follows:

• Application to the Honors Program (must be pre-approved by the faculty advisor)

• Enrollment in MATSCI150 Undergraduate Research and participation in an independent research project over three full quarters

• Completion of a faculty-approved thesis

• Participation in the MSE Research Symposium in Spring quarter, or a poster or oral presentation of thesis work at a Stanford Symposium/event or, at your faculty advisor’s discretion, in a comparable public event.
Since this requires three full quarters of research and a final written thesis and presentation following completion of the work, students must apply to the program no less than four quarters before their planned graduation date. Materials Science and Engineering majors pursuing a typical four-year graduation timeline should meet with an MSE Advisor no later than winter quarter of their junior year to receive information on the application process.
All requirements for the Honors Program are in addition to the standard undergraduate program requirements.

rules.name: To apply to the MATSCI Honors program
rules.desc:
• Application deadlines and additional information can be found here.

• Have an overall GPA of 3.700 or higher (as listed at the end of the unofficial transcript) at the time of application.

• Have taken ENGR 50 and at least six MATSCI courses.

• Seek out a Faculty Research Advisor and agree on a proposed research topic.

• Complete and submit an Honors Program application package, which includes the following three documents:

• MSE Honors Application form

• Summary of the proposed research (300–500 words)

• Unofficial transcript

rules.name: To complete the MATSCI Honors program
rules.desc:
• Overall GPA of 3.7 or higher at the end of the quarter prior to degree conferral (calculated on the unofficial transcript).

• Complete at least three-quarters of research with a minimum of 9 units of MATSCI 150 (students may petition out-of-unit requirement with Faculty Advisor approval). All quarters must focus on the same topic. Maintain the same faculty advisor throughout, if possible.

• For detailed requirements see the MatSci Honors Program Guidelines.

• Present a poster presentation of thesis work at the MSE Research Symposium, or at a comparable public event. The Faculty Advisor needs to sign off on this requirement.

• Submit final drafts of an Honors thesis to two faculty readers (one must be your research advisor, and one must be an MSE faculty member/SoE Academic Council member) at least one month before graduation. Both must approve the thesis by completing the signature page.

• Submit to the MATSCI Student Services Office (Durand 104) and MSE UG Advising one copy of the Honors thesis and the signed signature page in electronic form at least one month before graduation.
